modules.title: Introduction to Python & Environment Setup
modules.description: This module introduces Python's history, philosophy, and common applications. Learners will set up their development environment, understand basic syntax, and write their first 'Hello World' program.
modules.importance: Setting up a proper development environment is the first critical step for any programmer. Understanding Python's basics provides the foundation for all subsequent learning and practical application.
objectives: Understand Python's role in modern technology
Install Python and a suitable IDE (e.g., VS Code)
Write and execute basic Python scripts
Understand Python's interactive mode
learning_outcomes: Successfully set up a Python development environment
Execute simple Python commands and scripts
Differentiate between Python versions and their implications
topics: Integrated Development Environments (IDEs) and text editors
evaluation_questions: How do you install Python on your operating system?
What is the purpose of an IDE in Python development?
Write a Python script that prints your name and age.

resources.title: Python Tutorial for Beginners - Full Course
The Python Tutorial - Official Documentation
How To Install Python 3 and Set Up a Local Programming Environment

practice_exercises: Install Python and an IDE of your choice (e.g., VS Code, PyCharm Community).
Write a Python script that prints a short poem or quote.
Experiment with the Python interactive shell to perform simple arithmetic operations.

modules.title: Python Fundamentals: Variables, Data Types, and Operators
modules.description: This module dives into the core building blocks of Python: variables, various data types (integers, floats, strings, booleans), and operators. Learners will understand how to store, manipulate, and combine data.
modules.importance: Understanding how to store and manipulate data is fundamental to all programming. These concepts are the bedrock for creating dynamic and interactive applications.
objectives: Declare and use variables correctly
Identify and utilize different Python data types
Perform operations using arithmetic, assignment, comparison, and logical operators
Understand type conversion
learning_outcomes: Effectively use variables to store information
Manipulate strings, numbers, and booleans
Write expressions using various operators to achieve desired results
topics: String data type and string manipulation
evaluation_questions: Explain the difference between an integer and a float in Python.
How do you concatenate two strings in Python?
Write a Python program that calculates the area of a rectangle given its length and width as variables.

resources.title: Python Variables, Data Types, and Operators Tutorial
Python Data Types - W3Schools
Basic Operators in Python

practice_exercises: Create variables for your name, age, and height. Print them in a formatted sentence.
Write a program that takes two numbers, performs addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, and prints the results.
Experiment with string methods like `.upper()`, `.lower()`, `.replace()`, and string slicing.

modules.title: Control Flow: Conditionals and Loops
modules.description: This module teaches how to control the flow of a program using conditional statements (if, elif, else) and various looping constructs (for, while). These are essential for making programs dynamic and responsive.
modules.importance: Control flow structures allow programs to make decisions and repeat actions, which is crucial for creating any non-trivial application, from simple scripts to complex software.
objectives: Implement conditional logic using if, elif, and else statements
Utilize for loops to iterate over sequences
Implement while loops for repetitive tasks based on a condition
Understand and use break and continue statements
learning_outcomes: Write programs that respond differently based on input or conditions
Automate repetitive tasks using loops
Control loop execution with break and continue
topics: The 'for' loop and iterating over sequences
Loop control statements: break, continue, pass
evaluation_questions: Explain when to use an 'if-elif-else' structure versus nested 'if' statements.
Write a 'for' loop that prints numbers from 1 to 10.
Write a 'while' loop that asks the user for input until they type 'quit'.

resources.title: Python If Else, For Loop, While Loop Tutorial
Python If...Else - W3Schools
Python For Loops - W3Schools

practice_exercises: Write a program that checks if a number is positive, negative, or zero.
Create a program that prints all even numbers from 1 to 20 using a 'for' loop.
Build a simple guessing game where the user has to guess a secret number within a certain number of attempts using a 'while' loop.

modules.title: Data Structures: Lists, Tuples, Dictionaries, and Sets
modules.description: This module introduces Python's fundamental built-in data structures: lists, tuples, dictionaries, and sets. Learners will understand their characteristics, when to use each, and how to manipulate them effectively.
modules.importance: Efficiently organizing and accessing data is paramount in programming. Mastering these data structures allows for robust and scalable data management within applications.
objectives: Understand the properties and use cases of lists, tuples, dictionaries, and sets
Perform common operations like adding, removing, and accessing elements
Differentiate between mutable and immutable data types
Utilize list comprehensions for concise list creation
learning_outcomes: Choose the appropriate data structure for a given problem
Manipulate data within lists, tuples, dictionaries, and sets
Write more efficient code using list comprehensions
topics: Lists: creation, indexing, slicing, methods (append, insert, remove, sort)
Dictionaries: creation, key-value pairs, accessing, adding, updating, deleting elements
Sets: creation, unique elements, set operations (union, intersection, difference)
evaluation_questions: When would you use a list instead of a tuple?
How do you add a new key-value pair to an existing dictionary?
Write a list comprehension that creates a list of squares for numbers from 1 to 5.

resources.title: Python Data Structures (Lists, Tuples, Dictionaries, Sets) Tutorial
Python Lists - W3Schools
Python Dictionaries - W3Schools

practice_exercises: Create a list of your favorite movies and print them. Add a new movie and remove an old one.
Create a dictionary representing a person with keys like 'name', 'age', 'city'. Access and modify some values.
Write a program that takes a list of numbers and returns a new list containing only the unique numbers using sets.

modules.title: Functions
modules.description: This module covers the concept of functions, which are reusable blocks of code. Learners will learn how to define, call, and pass arguments to functions, as well as understand scope and return values.
modules.importance: Functions are crucial for writing modular, organized, and reusable code. They improve readability, reduce redundancy, and make programs easier to debug and maintain.
objectives: Define and call functions with and without arguments
Understand positional and keyword arguments
Utilize default argument values
Understand variable scope (local vs. global)
Return values from functions
learning_outcomes: Write modular and reusable code using functions
Pass data to functions and receive results
Manage variable scope effectively
evaluation_questions: What is the purpose of a function in Python?
Explain the difference between positional and keyword arguments.
Write a function that takes two numbers as input and returns their sum.

resources.title: Python Functions Tutorial for Beginners
Python Functions - W3Schools
Defining Your Own Python Function

practice_exercises: Write a function that calculates the factorial of a given number.
Create a function that takes a list of numbers and returns the largest number in the list.
Build a simple calculator function that takes two numbers and an operator (+, -, *, /) and returns the result.

modules.title: File I/O and Error Handling
modules.description: This module teaches how to interact with files (read from and write to them) and how to handle errors gracefully using try-except blocks. These skills are vital for creating robust applications that interact with external data.
modules.importance: Most real-world applications need to store and retrieve data from files. Robust error handling ensures that programs don't crash unexpectedly, providing a better user experience and easier debugging.
objectives: Open, read, and write to text files
Understand different file modes (read, write, append)
Use the 'with' statement for automatic file closing
Implement try-except blocks to handle common errors
Understand different types of exceptions
learning_outcomes: Read data from and write data to files
Prevent program crashes using exception handling
Create more resilient and user-friendly applications
topics: File modes (r, w, a, r+, w+, a+)
evaluation_questions: What is the advantage of using the 'with' statement for file operations?
How do you handle a 'FileNotFoundError' in Python?
Write a program that reads a line from a file named 'data.txt' and prints it.

resources.title: Python File I/O and Exception Handling Tutorial
Python File Handling - W3Schools
Python Try Except - W3Schools

practice_exercises: Create a text file, write a few lines of text into it, then read the entire content and print it.
Write a program that tries to open a non-existent file and handles the 'FileNotFoundError' gracefully.
Create a simple 'to-do list' program that allows users to add tasks to a file and view all tasks from the file.

modules.title: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) Basics
modules.description: This module introduces the fundamental concepts of Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) in Python. Learners will understand classes, objects, attributes, and methods, laying the groundwork for more complex software design.
modules.importance: OOP is a powerful paradigm for structuring complex applications, promoting code reusability, maintainability, and scalability. It's a core concept in modern software development.
objectives: Understand the concepts of classes and objects
Define classes with attributes and methods
Create instances of classes (objects)
Understand the 'self' keyword and the '__init__' method
Grasp basic principles like encapsulation
learning_outcomes: Design and implement simple classes in Python
Create and interact with objects
Organize code using an object-oriented approach
topics: Encapsulation (public vs. private members - Pythonic way)
evaluation_questions: Explain the difference between a class and an object.
What is the purpose of the '__init__' method in a Python class?
Create a simple 'Car' class with attributes like 'make', 'model', and a method to display car information.

resources.title: Python OOP Tutorial for Beginners
Python Classes and Objects - W3Schools
Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) in Python 3

practice_exercises: Design a 'Dog' class with attributes like 'name' and 'breed', and methods like 'bark()' and 'sit()'. Create a few dog objects.
Create a 'BankAccount' class with attributes 'account_number' and 'balance', and methods for 'deposit' and 'withdraw'.
Extend the 'Car' class to include a method that calculates the car's age based on its 'year_made' attribute.

modules.title: Modules and Packages
modules.description: This module teaches how to organize Python code into modules and packages, which are essential for managing larger projects. Learners will understand how to import and use code from other files and libraries.
modules.importance: As projects grow, organizing code into reusable modules and packages becomes critical for maintainability, collaboration, and avoiding naming conflicts. This is a cornerstone of professional Python development.
objectives: Understand the concept of modules and packages
Import modules and specific functions/variables from them
Create custom modules and use them in other scripts
Understand the Python Standard Library
learning_outcomes: Structure Python projects effectively using modules and packages
Utilize code from the Python Standard Library
Improve code reusability and organization
topics: Introduction to the Python Standard Library
evaluation_questions: What is the primary benefit of using modules in Python?
Explain the difference between 'import mymodule' and 'from mymodule import function_name'.
How would you structure a simple project with multiple Python files into a package?

resources.title: Python Modules and Packages Explained
Python Modules - W3Schools
Python Packages: An Introduction

practice_exercises: Create two Python files: `math_operations.py` with functions for addition and subtraction, and `main.py` that imports and uses these functions.
Organize a small project into a package structure with an `__init__.py` file and multiple modules.
Explore and use a module from the Python Standard Library, such as the `math` module or `random` module.

modules.title: Introduction to Libraries (e.g., Math, Random)
modules.description: This module introduces learners to using external libraries and built-in modules to extend Python's functionality. It focuses on practical examples with common libraries like `math` and `random`.
modules.importance: Python's strength lies in its vast ecosystem of libraries. Learning to leverage these libraries allows developers to perform complex tasks efficiently without reinventing the wheel, accelerating development.
objectives: Understand how to import and use functions from built-in modules
Utilize the `math` module for mathematical operations
Utilize the `random` module for generating random numbers
Explore other useful standard library modules (e.g., `datetime`, `os`)
learning_outcomes: Perform advanced mathematical calculations
Generate random data for simulations or games
Access system-level functionalities using standard libraries
topics: The `math` module (sqrt, ceil, floor, pi, etc.)
Using `pip` to install external packages (brief overview)
evaluation_questions: How do you generate a random integer between 1 and 10 using the `random` module?
What is the purpose of the `math.sqrt()` function?
Briefly explain what `pip` is used for.

resources.title: Python Standard Library Tutorial
The Python Standard Library - Official Docs
Python Random Module

practice_exercises: Write a program that calculates the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle given its two sides using the `math` module.
Create a simple dice rolling simulator that generates random numbers between 1 and 6.
Write a program that generates a random password of a specified length using characters from a string.

modules.title: Basic Project: Command-Line Application
modules.description: This capstone module guides learners through building a complete, albeit simple, command-line application. It integrates all previously learned concepts into a practical project, solidifying understanding.
modules.importance: Applying learned concepts in a real project is the most effective way to consolidate knowledge and develop problem-solving skills. It provides tangible proof of learning and builds confidence.
objectives: Design a simple command-line application
Integrate functions, data structures, file I/O, and error handling
Plan and structure a small Python project
Debug and refine a complete application
learning_outcomes: Successfully build a functional command-line application
Demonstrate proficiency in core Python concepts
Gain experience in project planning and execution
topics: Storing data (e.g., in a list or file)
Basic error handling for user input
evaluation_questions: Describe the main components of your command-line application.
How did you handle user input and potential errors in your project?
What was the most challenging part of building this application, and how did you overcome it?

resources.title: Build a Command Line Application with Python
How to Build a Command Line Interface (CLI) in Python
Python CLI Tutorial: Build a Command-Line Tool

practice_exercises: Build a simple 'Contact Book' application that allows users to add, view, and delete contacts (stored in a file).
Create a 'Quiz Game' where questions and answers are loaded from a file, and the user's score is tracked.
Develop a 'Unit Converter' that converts between different units (e.g., Celsius to Fahrenheit, meters to feet) based on user input.

modules.title: Python Programming for Data Science
modules.description: This module covers the fundamental concepts of Python programming essential for data science and machine learning. It includes data structures, control flow, functions, and an introduction to key libraries like NumPy and Pandas for data manipulation.
modules.outcome: Learners will be proficient in Python for data handling and ready to apply it to machine learning tasks.
modules.importance: Python is the most widely used programming language in AI/ML due to its extensive libraries and community support. A strong foundation is crucial for implementing algorithms and managing data.
objectives: Understand Python syntax and basic programming constructs.
Learn to use Python data structures (lists, dictionaries, tuples, sets).
Master NumPy for numerical operations and array manipulation.
Utilize Pandas for data loading, cleaning, and analysis.
Perform basic data visualization with Matplotlib/Seaborn.
learning_outcomes: Write clean and efficient Python code.
Manipulate data using NumPy arrays and Pandas DataFrames.
Apply basic statistical operations to datasets.
Create simple plots to visualize data distributions.
topics: Python basics (variables, data types, operators, control flow)
Pandas DataFrames (creation, selection, filtering, grouping, merging)
evaluation_questions: How do you create a Pandas DataFrame from a dictionary?
Explain the difference between a NumPy array and a Python list.
Write a Python function to calculate the mean of a list of numbers.
practice_exercises: Load a CSV file into a Pandas DataFrame, clean missing values, and calculate descriptive statistics.
Use NumPy to perform matrix multiplication and element-wise operations on two arrays.
Create a scatter plot of two columns from your DataFrame using Matplotlib.

resources.title: YouTube: Python Programming for Data Science Tutorial
Web: Learn Python Programming for Data Science

modules.title: Mathematics Foundations for Machine Learning
modules.description: This module introduces the essential mathematical concepts underpinning machine learning algorithms. It covers linear algebra, calculus, and statistics, providing the theoretical background necessary to understand how ML models work.
modules.outcome: Learners will grasp the core mathematical principles behind ML, enabling them to understand algorithm mechanics and interpret results.
modules.importance: A solid understanding of mathematics is crucial for comprehending the inner workings of ML algorithms, debugging models, and developing new ones. It moves beyond just using libraries to truly understanding the science.
objectives: Understand vector and matrix operations in linear algebra.
Grasp basic concepts of differential calculus relevant to optimization.
Learn fundamental probability theory and statistical concepts.
Apply statistical measures to data analysis.
learning_outcomes: Perform vector and matrix manipulations.
Understand gradients and derivatives in the context of optimization.
Interpret probability distributions and statistical tests.
Calculate and interpret mean, median, mode, variance, and standard deviation.
topics: Linear Algebra: Vectors, Matrices, Dot Product, Matrix Multiplication, Inverse, Determinant
Statistics: Mean, Median, Mode, Variance, Standard Deviation, Probability Distributions (Normal, Bernoulli)
evaluation_questions: Explain the concept of a gradient in the context of machine learning.
What is the difference between variance and standard deviation?
Given two vectors, how would you calculate their dot product?
practice_exercises: Implement a Python function to calculate the dot product of two vectors.
Given a dataset, calculate its mean, median, and standard deviation using NumPy.
Sketch the graph of a simple function and its derivative.

resources.title: YouTube: Mathematics Foundations for Machine Learning Tutorial
Web: Learn Mathematics Foundations for Machine Learning

modules.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
modules.description: This module provides a high-level overview of machine learning, defining its core concepts, types (supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement), and typical workflow. It introduces the Scikit-learn library for practical implementation.
modules.outcome: Learners will understand the fundamental principles of machine learning and be able to identify appropriate ML tasks and tools.
modules.importance: This module sets the stage for all subsequent ML topics, providing the foundational vocabulary and conceptual framework necessary to navigate the field.
objectives: Define machine learning and its main paradigms.
Understand the typical machine learning workflow.
Identify different types of machine learning problems.
Get acquainted with the Scikit-learn library for basic ML tasks.
learning_outcomes: Distinguish between supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning.
Outline the steps involved in a machine learning project.
Load and prepare a dataset for a simple ML model using Scikit-learn.
Train and make predictions with a basic Scikit-learn model.
topics: Supervised Learning vs. Unsupervised Learning vs. Reinforcement Learning
Machine Learning Workflow (Data Collection, Preprocessing, Model Training, Evaluation, Deployment)
evaluation_questions: What is the primary difference between supervised and unsupervised learning?
List the typical steps in a machine learning project.
How does Scikit-learn simplify the process of building ML models?
practice_exercises: Load a built-in dataset from Scikit-learn (e.g., Iris or Boston housing) and inspect its features.
Split a dataset into training and testing sets using Scikit-learn's `train_test_split`.
Train a dummy classifier or regressor on a small dataset and make predictions.

resources.title: YouTube: Introduction to Machine Learning Tutorial
Web: Learn Introduction to Machine Learning

modules.title: Data Preprocessing and Feature Engineering
modules.description: This module focuses on preparing raw data for machine learning models. It covers techniques for handling missing values, encoding categorical data, scaling numerical features, and creating new features to improve model performance.
modules.outcome: Learners will be able to effectively preprocess and engineer features from raw data, making it suitable for various ML algorithms.
modules.importance: High-quality data is paramount for effective machine learning. Proper preprocessing and feature engineering can significantly impact model accuracy and generalization, often more than the choice of algorithm itself.
objectives: Identify and handle missing data.
Encode categorical variables into numerical representations.
Scale numerical features appropriately.
Understand the importance of feature engineering and create new features.
Handle outliers and imbalanced datasets (introduction).
learning_outcomes: Apply different strategies for imputing missing values.
Use one-hot encoding and label encoding for categorical data.
Implement standardization and normalization for numerical features.
Design and implement simple new features from existing ones.
Explain the impact of data scaling on model performance.
topics: Missing Data Imputation (mean, median, mode, forward/backward fill)
evaluation_questions: When would you use one-hot encoding versus label encoding?
Explain the difference between standardization and normalization.
Describe a scenario where feature engineering would be beneficial.
practice_exercises: Take a dataset with missing values and categorical features, then apply appropriate imputation and encoding techniques.
Apply both standardization and normalization to a numerical feature and observe the changes.
Create a new feature by combining two existing features (e.g., ratio, product) and explain its potential utility.

resources.title: YouTube: Data Preprocessing and Feature Engineering Tutorial
Web: Learn Data Preprocessing and Feature Engineering

modules.title: Supervised Learning: Regression
modules.description: This module delves into regression algorithms, a core type of supervised learning used for predicting continuous numerical values. It covers Linear Regression, Polynomial Regression, and introduces evaluation metrics specific to regression tasks.
modules.outcome: Learners will be able to build, train, and evaluate regression models to predict continuous outcomes.
modules.importance: Regression is fundamental for predicting quantities like house prices, stock values, or temperature. It's a widely applicable technique across many industries.
objectives: Understand the principles of Linear Regression.
Implement Simple and Multiple Linear Regression models.
Explore Polynomial Regression for non-linear relationships.
Evaluate regression models using metrics like MAE, MSE, RMSE, and R-squared.
learning_outcomes: Train a Linear Regression model using Scikit-learn.
Interpret the coefficients of a linear model.
Apply Polynomial Regression to capture non-linear patterns.
Calculate and interpret common regression evaluation metrics.
topics: Regression Evaluation Metrics: MAE, MSE, RMSE, R-squared
evaluation_questions: What is the primary goal of a regression model?
Explain the difference between MSE and R-squared.
When would you consider using Polynomial Regression over Linear Regression?
practice_exercises: Build a Linear Regression model to predict house prices based on features like size and number of bedrooms.
Experiment with Polynomial Regression on a dataset with a clear non-linear relationship and compare its performance to Linear Regression.
Calculate and interpret MAE, MSE, and R-squared for your regression models.

resources.title: YouTube: Supervised Learning: Regression Tutorial
Web: Learn Supervised Learning: Regression

modules.title: Supervised Learning: Classification
modules.description: This module explores classification algorithms, another fundamental type of supervised learning used for predicting categorical labels. It covers Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Support Vector Machines (SVMs), and introduces classification-specific evaluation metrics.
modules.outcome: Learners will be able to build, train, and evaluate classification models to predict discrete categories.
modules.importance: Classification is essential for tasks like spam detection, image recognition, medical diagnosis, and customer churn prediction. It's one of the most common applications of machine learning.
objectives: Understand the principles of Logistic Regression.
Implement Decision Tree classifiers and understand their decision-making process.
Grasp the concept of Support Vector Machines (SVMs).
Evaluate classification models using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrices.
learning_outcomes: Train Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and SVM models using Scikit-learn.
Interpret the output of a confusion matrix.
Calculate and interpret precision, recall, and F1-score.
Choose an appropriate classification algorithm for a given problem.
topics: Classification Evaluation Metrics: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score, Confusion Matrix
evaluation_questions: What is the main difference between Logistic Regression and Linear Regression?
Explain how a Decision Tree makes predictions.
When would precision be a more important metric than recall?
practice_exercises: Build a Logistic Regression model to classify emails as spam or not spam.
Train a Decision Tree classifier on the Iris dataset and visualize the tree.
Compare the performance of Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, and a simple SVM on a binary classification task using multiple evaluation metrics.

resources.title: YouTube: Supervised Learning: Classification Tutorial
Web: Learn Supervised Learning: Classification

modules.title: Unsupervised Learning: Clustering and Dimensionality Reduction
modules.description: This module introduces unsupervised learning techniques, which are used to find patterns in data without explicit labels. It covers clustering algorithms like K-Means and dimensionality reduction techniques like Principal Component Analysis (PCA).
modules.outcome: Learners will be able to apply unsupervised learning methods to discover hidden structures in data and reduce data complexity.
modules.importance: Unsupervised learning is crucial for tasks like customer segmentation, anomaly detection, and data compression, especially when labeled data is scarce or expensive to obtain.
objectives: Understand the concept of unsupervised learning.
Implement K-Means clustering and interpret its results.
Grasp the principles of Principal Component Analysis (PCA).
Apply PCA for dimensionality reduction and visualization.
learning_outcomes: Perform K-Means clustering on a dataset and visualize the clusters.
Determine an appropriate number of clusters using methods like the elbow method.
Apply PCA to reduce the number of features in a dataset.
Explain the trade-offs of dimensionality reduction.
topics: Clustering: K-Means Algorithm (theory and implementation), Elbow Method
Dimensionality Reduction: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) - theory and implementation
evaluation_questions: How does K-Means clustering work?
What is the primary goal of Principal Component Analysis?
Describe a real-world application for clustering.
practice_exercises: Apply K-Means clustering to a customer dataset to identify distinct customer segments.
Use PCA to reduce the dimensionality of a high-dimensional dataset (e.g., digits dataset) and visualize the principal components.
Experiment with different numbers of clusters for K-Means and evaluate the results using the elbow method.

resources.title: YouTube: Unsupervised Learning: Clustering and Dimensionality Reduction Tutorial
Web: Learn Unsupervised Learning: Clustering and Dimensionality Reduction

modules.title: Model Evaluation, Selection, and Hyperparameter Tuning
modules.description: This module consolidates knowledge on how to rigorously evaluate, select, and optimize machine learning models. It covers cross-validation, hyperparameter tuning techniques, and strategies to prevent overfitting and underfitting.
modules.outcome: Learners will be able to systematically evaluate model performance, select the best model, and fine-tune its hyperparameters for optimal results.
modules.importance: Proper model evaluation and tuning are critical for building robust and generalizable ML systems. Without these, models may perform poorly on new, unseen data.
objectives: Understand the importance of cross-validation.
Implement various cross-validation strategies.
Learn about hyperparameter tuning techniques like Grid Search and Random Search.
Identify and address overfitting and underfitting.
Understand regularization techniques (L1, L2) conceptually.
learning_outcomes: Apply K-Fold cross-validation to assess model stability.
Use GridSearchCV or RandomizedSearchCV to find optimal hyperparameters.
Diagnose overfitting and underfitting in models.
Implement basic regularization in linear models.
Select the best model based on appropriate evaluation metrics.
topics: Hyperparameter Tuning: Grid Search, Random Search
evaluation_questions: Why is cross-validation important for model evaluation?
Explain the difference between a hyperparameter and a model parameter.
How can you mitigate overfitting in a machine learning model?

lessons.title: Model Evaluation and Hyperparameter Tuning Tutorial

practice_exercises: Apply K-Fold cross-validation to a classification model and report the average performance metrics.
Use GridSearchCV to find the optimal hyperparameters for a Decision Tree classifier on a given dataset.
Train a regularized linear model (e.g., Ridge or Lasso Regression) and compare its performance to a non-regularized model.

resources.title: YouTube: Model Evaluation, Selection, and Hyperparameter Tuning Tutorial
Web: Learn Model Evaluation, Selection, and Hyperparameter Tuning

modules.title: Introduction to Deep Learning
modules.description: This module provides an introduction to the exciting field of deep learning, covering the basics of neural networks, activation functions, backpropagation (conceptual), and building simple models using TensorFlow/Keras.
modules.outcome: Learners will understand the foundational concepts of deep learning and be able to build and train basic neural networks.
modules.importance: Deep learning has revolutionized fields like computer vision and natural language processing. Understanding its basics is essential for anyone pursuing advanced AI/ML.
objectives: Understand the architecture of a basic Artificial Neural Network (ANN).
Grasp the role of activation functions.
Understand the concept of backpropagation (high-level).
Build and train a simple feedforward neural network using Keras/TensorFlow.
Understand the difference between deep learning and traditional machine learning.
learning_outcomes: Explain the components of a neuron and a neural network.
Choose appropriate activation functions for different layers.
Implement a multi-layer perceptron for a classification task.
Evaluate the performance of a deep learning model.
Differentiate between shallow and deep neural networks.
topics: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs): Neurons, Layers, Weights, Biases
Introduction to Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) - conceptual
evaluation_questions: Describe the basic structure of an artificial neuron.
What is the purpose of an activation function in a neural network?
How does deep learning differ from traditional machine learning in its approach to feature engineering?
practice_exercises: Build a simple feedforward neural network using Keras to classify images from the Fashion MNIST dataset.
Experiment with different activation functions and optimizers in your neural network and observe their impact on performance.
Implement a multi-layer perceptron for a binary classification task and compare its performance to a Logistic Regression model.
